lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Saturday, October third.
Today: a weak September jobs report, the world's biggest economies agree to release emergency oil, and a reported war council at Camp David.
Plus new A.I. models, a food outbreak that officials have now closed, and baseball's division series. Let's go.

segments.strap: REPORT: TRUMP AIDES MEET AT CAMP DAVID ON IRAN
segments.headline: Iran, day two hundred seventeen

graphic.title: Iran war, day 217
bullets: Axios: Camp David meeting as talks stall
Trump reported weighing renewed major combat
W.S.J.: third carrier, up to 10,000 troops
New Treasury sanctions on Iran's auto and rail sectors

lines.text: On day two hundred seventeen of the Iran war, Axios reports that Trump's senior national-security aides met at Camp David on Iran and Yemen, as negotiations stalled. Axios says Trump is considering renewed major combat operations. That is a report, not an announcement.

Other outlets describe a buildup. The Wall Street Journal reports a third U.S. carrier and nine to ten thousand more troops, with Patriot batteries going to Saudi Arabia and Qatar. Sources differ on the troop number.
New Treasury sanctions hit Iran's auto and rail sectors. And Iran struck a fifth tanker in the Strait of Hormuz in three days.

In Britain, a twenty-five-year-old was arrested on suspicion of terrorism preparation, tied to the R.A.F. Fairford base. The A.P. says U.S. and British leaders suggested Iran was involved in two incidents this week, but it presented no evidence. That is a claim.

segments.strap: G7 AGREES 100 MILLION BARREL OIL RELEASE; BRENT $102.25
segments.headline: Emergency oil

graphic.title: G7 opens the reserves
bullets: Released over four months, diesel first
G7 pledges against export limits between members
China suspends fuel exports until further notice
W.T.I. fell nearly 4% on Friday

lines.text: G7 leaders agreed to a coordinated release of one hundred million barrels of oil from reserves, over four months. A lot of it is diesel, front-loaded into the first twenty days.
The G7 also pledged not to restrict exports between its members. That follows China's suspension of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel exports, which it says lasts until further notice.
Friday's prices: Brent settled at one hundred two dollars and twenty-five cents, almost unchanged. U.S. crude fell nearly four percent.

One more number, from Oilprice dot com. Physical Dated Brent is reported above one hundred twenty dollars. That is a claim, and it is far above the futures price. The physical market is tighter than the screen suggests.

graphic.title: September jobs
bullets: Wages +0.1% on the month, +3.0% on the year
10-year yield about 5.18%

lines.text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports employers added twenty-nine thousand jobs in September. Forecasts were near eighty-four thousand. Unemployment rose to four point two percent.
July and August were revised down by a combined sixty thousand jobs. Hourly pay rose a tenth of a percent in the month, and three percent over the year.
Stocks still rose. The S&P five hundred gained point seven percent to seven thousand seven hundred twenty-two. The Dow added half a percent. The Nasdaq rose one point two.

Treasury yields fell after the report, then pulled back. The ten-year is near five point one eight percent, after its run to the highest since two thousand two. Coverage says the numbers raise the odds the Fed holds rates at its late-October meeting.
Congress also avoided a shutdown. Funding now runs through December eleventh.

segments.strap: RUSSIAN STRIKES HIT KYIV; PUTIN REPEATS KALININGRAD THREAT
segments.headline: Russia and Ukraine

graphic.title: War in Ukraine
bullets: Kyiv strikes: one killed, two hurt
Two Dnipro bridges closed
Drone hit a school with children sheltering
Putin repeats Kaliningrad nuclear threat

lines.text: Russian strikes on Kyiv killed one person and injured two, and closed two bridges over the Dnipro. A drone hit a school while children were sheltering inside.
Vladimir Putin repeated his threat to use nuclear weapons over Kaliningrad. That is a statement of intent, not an action.

segments.strap: OPENAI LAUNCHES GPT-6.1 SOL; GOOGLE GATES GEMINI 4 ARGON
segments.headline: A week of new models

graphic.title: The week in A.I.
bullets: OpenAI: GPT-6.1 Sol at $2 / $10 per million tokens
OpenAI reported scrapping GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns
Google: Gemini 4 Argon to trusted defenders first
Anthropic IPO reported for mid-November

lines.text: OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Sol, priced at two dollars and ten dollars per million tokens. That is one-fifth the price of GPT-6 Astra, with similar results on agentic coding. It also added a five-hundred-dollar plan and an automation product called Dots.

Reports say OpenAI scrapped a bigger model, GPT-6.1 Astra, over internal safety and alignment concerns. Google released Gemini 4 Argon first to trusted cyber defenders, claiming it can find, validate and fix serious software flaws on its own.
Two labs held back capability in the same week. Reportedly, Bloomberg says Anthropic is targeting an I.P.O. in mid-November.
Disclosure: Anthropic makes the model that helps write this show.

segments.strap: JUDGE PAUSES BORDER WALL IN BIG BEND; SPRINGFIELD PLANT CLOSES
segments.headline: Around the country

graphic.title: Around the country
bullets: Judge pauses Big Bend border construction
Supreme Court takes major immigration case
Springfield, Ohio: ~1,400 laid off
Vicksburg, Miss.: ransomware shuts city systems

lines.text: The A.P. reports a federal judge, Kathleen Cardone, temporarily blocked border-wall construction in Texas' Big Bend region while a challenge goes forward. The work is part of a forty-six billion dollar border program.
The Supreme Court agreed Thursday to take up a major case central to the administration's immigration crackdown. Arguments are expected in the coming months.

In Springfield, Ohio, the A.P. says nearly fourteen hundred workers lost their jobs as the former Navistar truck plant closed. One worker told the A.P. five grocery items now cost what a full cart once did. That is one person's account.
And in Vicksburg, Mississippi, a ransomware attack forced the city's computers offline. Nine-one-one, police and fire are still running.

segments.strap: FDA CLOSES CYCLOSPORA PROBE: 12,883 ILLNESSES, TWO DEATHS
segments.headline: Lettuce outbreak closed

graphic.title: Cyclospora investigation closed
bullets: Linked to iceberg lettuce from central Mexico
Two positive environmental samples
Contamination route not established
Salmonella outbreak from jalapenos also closed: 488 cases

lines.text: The F.D.A. closed its investigation of a Cyclospora outbreak tied to recalled iceberg lettuce from central Mexico. The final count is twelve thousand eight hundred eighty-three illnesses, five hundred seventy hospitalizations and two deaths, across twenty-one states.

Two environmental samples tested positive, one from a processing plant's wastewater tank and one from a grower's drainage ditch. But the F.D.A. says it could not establish how the contamination happened.

A second outbreak is also closed: Salmonella Javiana, linked to jalapenos from Sinaloa, with four hundred eighty-eight cases in thirty-four states. The last Cyclospora illness began August seventeenth.

segments.strap: HURRICANES RACHEL AND NOLO IN THE PACIFIC; SOCAL HEAT WAVE
segments.headline: Two Pacific hurricanes

graphic.title: Pacific storms and heat
bullets: Rachel weakening, moving west at 5 mph
Nolo strengthening, moving west at 7 mph
No active Atlantic storms
S. California heat wave: low 90s to mid-100s

lines.text: The National Hurricane Center lists two hurricanes in the Eastern Pacific. Rachel has winds of one hundred miles an hour, down from a Category Three, and is moving west at five.
Nolo has winds of eighty-five miles an hour and is strengthening, moving west at seven. The Atlantic has no active storms.

On land, Southern California is in a long October heat wave. AccuWeather says highs run from the low nineties to the mid-one-hundreds, with low humidity and gusty winds raising fire risk. Federal forecasters also see above-normal fire potential in north Texas and western Oklahoma.

segments.strap: BRAVES-DODGERS NLDS OPENS TODAY; DANIELS OUT FOR LONDON
segments.headline: Playoffs and football

graphic.title: Baseball and football
bullets: Braves at Dodgers, Game 1: 4 p.m. ET
Triple-digit heat forecast at Dodger Stadium
Chris Sale unavailable before Game 2
Commanders QB Daniels out; Mariota starts in London

lines.text: The Braves and Dodgers open the National League Division Series today at four p.m. Eastern, at Dodger Stadium. M.L.B. says triple-digit heat is forecast. Atlanta's Chris Sale is unavailable before Game Two.
In the N.F.L., the Commanders ruled out quarterback Jayden Daniels with an elbow injury for Sunday's game against the Colts in London. Coach Dan Quinn says Marcus Mariota will start.
Saturday's college football slate is full, with injury lists posted for Nebraska, Boise State and others.

segments.strap: FALCON HEAVY FLIES FIRST N.R.O. MISSION; CREW-13 AT STATION
segments.headline: Launch roundup

graphic.title: Three launches in two days
bullets: Crew-13 launched to the station on time Oct. 1
Transporter-18 carries NASA's SPRITE observatory
Falcon Heavy flies NROL-97, first N.R.O. Falcon Heavy
Starlink V3 Starship result not yet confirmed

lines.text: A busy few days for SpaceX. Crew Thirteen launched to the space station on time Thursday, commanded by Jessica Watkins. Transporter Eighteen flew the same day from Vandenberg with NASA's SPRITE observatory.
Friday, a Falcon Heavy launched N.R.O.L. ninety-seven, the first Falcon Heavy flight for the National Reconnaissance Office.

segments.strap: TESLA Q3 DELIVERIES 486,532; PARAMOUNT-WARNER CLOSE OCT. 6
segments.headline: Business and the box office

graphic.title: Deals and weekend film
bullets: Tesla full Q3 results Oct. 21
Paramount-Warner Bros. close reported for Oct. 6
Box office: Verity opens, ~$27M projected
Social estimate ~$35M; unconfirmed

lines.text: Tesla reports it built four hundred sixty-four thousand vehicles in the third quarter and delivered four hundred eighty-six thousand five hundred thirty-two. It deployed thirteen point seven gigawatt-hours of energy storage. Full results come October twenty-first.
The roughly eighty-one billion dollar Paramount and Warner Bros. merger is still reported to close Tuesday, October sixth.

At the box office, preview sites project about twenty-seven million dollars for the film Verity this weekend. One social-media poster guesses closer to thirty-five. That is an estimate, not a final number.
